images.title: Portail d'entrée du Castel Béranger (Hector Guimard)
images.author: Jean-Pierre Dalbéra
images.shows: Guimard whiplash wrought-iron entrance gate (copper + blue-green iron) with sculpted stone surround -- the canonical Art Nouveau ironwork reference

images.title: Castel Béranger, facade ensemble (Hector Guimard)
images.author: Greudin
images.shows: Full multi-storey facade in mixed brick/stone with irregular bay projections, oriels and balconies -- mild oblique angle, some tree obstruction

images.title: Édicule Guimard, Metro Porte Dauphine canopy
images.author: Moonik
images.street: Place du Maréchal-de-Lattre-de-Tassigny (Porte Dauphine), 16e arrondissement, Paris
images.shows: Guimard's cast-iron whiplash canopy structure with amber glass panels -- the definitive Art Nouveau ironwork motif in built form

images.title: Synagogue de la rue Pavée (Hector Guimard)
images.author: Greudin
images.shows: Tall narrow reinforced-concrete facade with vertically fluted stone piers rising past the upper floors -- steep raking angle limits legibility

images.title: Hôtel Mezzara (Hector Guimard)
images.author: Henry Salomé
images.shows: Frontal townhouse facade with a full-height projecting central bay carried up past the cornice into a curved gable, plus a whiplash wrought-iron balcony rail

images.title: Immeuble Lavirotte, 29 avenue Rapp
images.author: Polymagou
images.shows: Sauciflard sandstone/brick facade with projecting sculpted balconies and an oriel carried up into a mansard dormer above the cornice line -- ground-floor tree obstruction, upper facade clean

images.title: 29 avenue Rapp, historic photograph (1918)
images.author: Charles Lansiaux
images.shows: Period documentary view of the Lavirotte facade's projecting oriel/loggia stack above the cornice, near contemporary with construction -- trees obscure the ground floor

images.title: 26 rue Vavin (Henri Sauvage)
images.author: GFreihalter
images.shows: The canonical Sauvage rue Vavin stepped ('à gradins') facade in white ceramic tile, terraces set back above the lower floors -- clean frontal view

images.title: 26 rue Vavin, stepped terraces (Henri Sauvage)
images.author: O.Taris
images.shows: Upward oblique view making the planted setback terraces of the gradins facade legible in profile -- steep angle, not a frontal read

images.title: Immeubles construits par Henri Sauvage au 22 rue Vavin (1918)
images.author: Léon Auguste
images.shows: Historic autochrome-derived plate of an earlier Sauvage stepped facade at 22 rue Vavin -- oblique, damaged/spotted emulsion, hard to read cleanly but valuable as a period record

images.title: Immeuble d'angle, 1 rue Boulard
images.author: Mbzt
images.street: 1 rue Boulard (angle 11 rue Froidevaux), 14e arrondissement, Paris
images.shows: Corner Art Nouveau apartment building (architect Léon Boucher) with continuous stacked curved balconies/oriels projecting from the facade up to and past the cornice

images.title: Studio Building, rue La Fontaine (Henri Sauvage)
images.author: jsmaur
images.street: rue La Fontaine / rue du Docteur-Blanche, 16e arrondissement, Paris
images.shows: Later Sauvage work in glazed brick with setback terraces and projecting balconies well above the cornice line -- steep upward angle but structure is legible

images.title: 7 rue Trétaigne, architects' signature plaque (Sauvage et Sarazin)
images.author: Remi Mathis
images.shows: Incised 'Sauvage et Sarazin Architectes 1904' signature plaque next to a ceramic-mosaic doorway -- confirms attribution and date but is a close detail, not a facade read

notes: Guimard whiplash ironwork is well covered (Castel Béranger gate, Metro Porte Dauphine canopy, Hôtel Mezzara balcony). Sauvage's rue Vavin stepped/gradins facade is covered by both a clean frontal shot and a period 1918 photograph of the neighbouring 22 rue Vavin building (poor quality, kept only for historic-document value). Projections carrying above the cornice line are evidenced by Hôtel Mezzara, Immeuble Lavirotte (29 avenue Rapp), 1 rue Boulard, and Sauvage's later Studio Building. The Lavirotte facade shots are tree-obstructed at ground level in both the modern and 1918 photographs -- no untreed frontal alternative was found on Commons at search time. The rue Pavée synagogue (Guimard) is only available at a steep raking angle on Commons; kept as partial quality since no better frontal shot surfaced. No image was guessed at for construction date where Commons metadata did not give one; dates above come from Commons file descriptions/categories, not independently verified against building permit records.
